title: (Working Paper) Good Faith Design: Religion as a Resource for Technologists
measurement_description: The paper does not benchmark Large Language Models. Instead, it conducts a qualitative interview study with 48 religious individuals and experts across 11 faiths to evaluate how religious people conceptualize, experience, and imagine digital technologies, focusing on their perceptions of secular embeddings in the tech industry and their desires for future technology design.
findings: Religious stakeholders perceive modern technology and its creators as holding non-neutral 'secular' biases, which leads to feelings of exclusion and unintended harms (e.g., algorithmic radicalization, biased datasets). Instead of hyper-individualized AI agents or tech-solutionism, religious users desire technologies that preserve human relationships, embrace humility and uncertainty, provide space for rest and spiritual work, acknowledge physical embodiedness, and foster prosocial community ties. Based on these findings, the authors propose six religiously informed design values for technologists: wonder, humility, space, embodiedness, community, and eternity.
